tts_summary: Here is your intraday alert. Marvell Technology shares are spiking after the company held an analyst meeting this morning with one of the most bullish AI data center outlooks we have seen from any company in the space. Let's get into the numbers because they matter. Marvell guided its fiscal 2031 sales to approximately 80 billion dollars. The Street was sitting at roughly 43 billion. That is not a small beat — that is nearly double consensus. Management also boosted its fiscal 2028 outlook, and for context, Marvell is expected to post around 3.1 billion dollars in sales in its fiscal third quarter ending in October. So the 80 billion dollar number is a very long-duration call, but the direction is unmistakably bullish. On the macro data center capex picture, Marvell said the entire tech industry spent more than 700 billion dollars on data center infrastructure in 2025. They expect that number to cross 1 trillion dollars this year, and they see a path to 3 trillion dollars by 2030 — implying roughly a 35 percent compound annual growth rate from 2025 levels. That is an extraordinary number and it adds another data point to the thesis that AI infrastructure spending is not slowing down. Marvell becomes the latest in a string of companies confirming that the capex upcycle in AI is accelerating, not decelerating. The read-through here is clearly positive for the broader semiconductor and AI infrastructure ecosystem — think networking chips, custom silicon, optical interconnects, and any name with meaningful hyperscaler exposure. The bull case is straightforward: if the people building AI chips and infrastructure are this confident in the spending trajectory, the secular demand story remains very much intact. The bear case is that fiscal 2031 guidance is a long way out, the numbers are hard to model, and stocks that spike on analyst day commentary can give back gains quickly if the broader tape turns. For now though, this is a clean, unambiguous positive catalyst for Marvell and a sentiment boost for the AI trade broadly. Stay focused and stay disciplined.
